statement: A rope 40 m long is cut into two pieces. One piece is 6 m longer than the other. How long is the longer piece?

choices.misconception: I found the shorter piece instead of the longer one.
I cut the rope in half and ignored the 6 m difference.
I cut the rope in half and then added the whole 6 m to one half.
I took the 6 m away from 40 m and called that the longer piece.

hints: Draw two bars, one 6 m longer than the other.
Take the extra 6 m off the longer bar so the two bars are equal. Share what is left of the rope between them, then put the 6 m back onto the longer one.
40 - 6 = 34 m shared equally gives 17 m for each equal bar.

solutions.reliable: Take the extra 6 m away: 40 - 6 = 34 m is shared equally, so each equal part is 17 m. The shorter piece is 17 m and the longer piece is 17 + 6 = 23 m. Check: 23 + 17 = 40 and 23 - 17 = 6. The transferable idea: in a sum-and-difference problem, remove the difference, halve, then add it back.
solutions.elegant: The answer is 3 m above the halfway point of 20 m, because the 6 m gap is split evenly on either side: 20 + 3 = 23 m.

whyOnTest: Sum and difference problems test a bar model, and each wrong length is one slip in that model.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
